description.narrative: Support to Environment and Climate in Kosovo-Idicative for 2014

Support to Environment and Climate in Kosovo-Idicative for 2014.
The development objective of the Programme is to contribute to improving the environmental conditions in Kosovo. The specific objectives of the Programme are: - To develop the capacity of the Ministry of Environment and Spatial Planning, the Inter-Ministerial Water Council, municipalities, civil society and other stakeholders in environmental monitoring and management. - To develop the capacity for implementation of environmental legislation, in compliance with EU directives. - To enhance the knowledge of Kosovo’s water resources and develop capacity for their improved management, and enhance resilience to environmental and climate change. - To enhance knowledge and protection of biodiversity and develop capacity for improved management of transboundary protected areas.

The development objective of the Programme is to contribute to improving the environmental conditions in Kosovo. The specific objectives of the Programme are: - To develop the capacity of the Ministry of Environment and Spatial Planning, the Inter-Ministerial Water Council, municipalities, civil society and other stakeholders in environmental monitoring and management. - To develop the capacity for implementation of environmental legislation, in compliance with EU directives. - To enhance the knowledge of Kosovo’s water resources and develop capacity for their improved management, and enhance resilience to environmental and climate change. - To enhance knowledge and protection of biodiversity and develop capacity for improved management of transboundary protected areas.

The Kosovo Environmental Program (KEP), primary focus was on enhancing the capabilities of key stakeholders, including the Ministry of Environment, Spatial Planning, and Infrastructure (MESPI) and the Inter-Ministerial Water Council (IMWC). However, KEP encountered significant challenges during implementation. MESPI faced resource shortages and lacked ownership of the project, leading to misunderstandings regarding contractual obligations. Political disruptions and staff turnover further impeded progress. Additionally, engaging stakeholders and addressing environmental and climate change challenges proved difficult. Retrospection suggests a need for a more focused approach, emphasizing political commitment, legislative approval, gender mainstreaming, and long-term sustainability.
Component 1. Strengthening the capacities of KEPA for environmental monitoring, evaluation, and reporting
The Ministry has successfully developed and established 48 environmental indicators, complete with comprehensive methodologies. The list of national environmental indicators received official approval. The publication of the "State of the Environment Report (2020)" based on these indicators disseminated crucial environmental insights. A comprehensive assessment of the existing Environmental Information System (EIS) led to the identification of needs and shortcomings. The Ministry compiled a comprehensive list of recommendations to address deficiencies and enhance the system's functionality. A technically sound proposal for EIS development was prepared. The "Environmental Information System Management " was meticulously crafted and subsequently approved. A technical specification was formulated, facilitating the acquisition of essential equipment for the geodatabase within the information system.
The Ministry efforts significantly improved environmental management and policy formulation. Dozens of reports grounded in environmental indicators informed policymaking in critical areas such as environment, air quality, water management, waste, and nature conservation. The overhaul of our data collection, processing, and reporting system streamlined operations. The Environmental Protection Agency of Kosovo (KEPA) fulfilled 100% of its reporting obligations to the European Environment Agency (EEA) and the Network for Monitoring and Observation (EIONET). Enhanced efficiency among KEAP staff was evident as they successfully managed air quality monitoring networks spanning 12 stations, oversaw water quality at 54 locations, and monitored water quantity at 27 stations. Additionally, they efficiently collected, processed, and reported waste data from 38 municipalities.
Increasing the efficiency of the KEPA staff for monitoring, evaluation, and reporting (the KEPA staff has successfully managed the air quality monitoring network with 12 stations, water quality monitoring with 54 locations, and water quantity monitoring in 27 stations, as well as collected, processed, and reported waste data for 38 municipalities).
Component 2. Preservation of biodiversity through the Red Book of Kosovo's animal species
The first general inventory of fauna in Kosovo was made. The red book of fauna in Kosovo was published for the first time and the only one so far. During the inventory of fauna for the drafting of the red book of fauna, two species new to science were discovered. The training of the staff of national parks, NGOs and other institutions for fauna monitoring has been done. The database for fauna species in Kosovo has been drawn up. Based on the red book of fauna, Administrative Instruction No. 12/2020 was drawn up for the declaration of protected and strictly protected wild species. Based on the data of the red book of fauna, 306 species of fauna were taken under protection for the first time in Kosovo. The red book of fauna has influenced the advancement of studies by students and different researchers in the field of fauna.
Component 3. Strengthening the management of transboundary natural areas
This program component played an essential role in advancing the sustainable development goals of National Parks Sharri and Bjeshket e Nemuna. The achievements, including the drafting of regulatory plans, the development of a management plan, study visits, and workshops, have collectively enhanced the capacity for effective and responsible management of these valuable natural assets. These efforts contribute to the broader mission of preserving the Kosovos natural heritage while fostering sustainable development in these regions.
Component 4. Establishment of the underground water monitoring network in Kosovo
The Kosovo Environmental Program (KEP) project represents a groundbreaking endeavor that inaugurated extensive research on the state of underground water within the Drini i Bardh basin. It encompasses both hydrometric measurements for real-time monitoring of underground water levels and research into physico-chemical water quality. The latter became possible through the installation of sensors that provide real-time data, which is seamlessly integrated into the Integrated Hydrometric Monitoring and Knowledge (IHMK) database.
Twenty-five locations within the Drini te Bardh Basin were strategically chosen to establish the network's foundation. A comprehensive rehabilitation effort was executed, paving the way for the installation of advanced monitoring facilities. These renovations set the stage for real-time hydrometric parameter measurements and the deployment of sensors at key stations. Beyond the Drini te Bardh Basin, the project extended its reach to the Iber-Morave-Lepenc river basins. Here, 20 existing stations underwent rehabilitation, receiving modern facilities for real-time hydrometric measurements and sensors to monitor water quality parameters.
The establishment of the underground water monitoring network in Kosovo, spearheaded by the KEP program has ushered in a new era of scientific exploration and resource management. Real-time hydrometric measurements and physico-chemical parameter tracking have become instrumental tools for comprehending and safeguarding the underground water resources of the Drini i Bardh basin. This pioneering initiative paves the way for sustainable environmental stewardship and data-informed decision-making.
Component 5 Strengthening capacities for the implementation of environmental legislation at the central and local level
The project KEP program, has been instrumental in undertakings and attempts made in enhancing the institutional capacities of the Ministry of Environment, Spatial Planning, and Infrastructure (MESPI) and municipalities, to effectively implement environmental legislation and regulations. Capacity assessment one of the fundamental actions undertaken by the KEP program was the comprehensive review and assessment of institutional capacities and deficiencies related to the implementation of environmental legislation. This assessment was conducted at both the central and local levels, providing valuable insights into the areas requiring improvement. When it comes to the alignment with European Union Directives, the KEP program extended its support to MESPI in producing a pivotal report evaluating the compatibility of national legislation with the directives and regulations of the European Union. This report served as the foundation for the development of concept documents pertaining to Environmental Impact Assessment, Strategic Environmental Assessment, and nature protection. In regard to development of by-laws, the program facilitated the creation of several critical by-laws that have significantly contributed to the realization of the project's primary objectives aimed at fostering a cleaner environment. Notable examples include the establishment of guidelines regarding the maximum allowable pollutant levels on the ground and the declaration of protected and strictly protected wild species.
To bolster the operational capabilities of municipalities, the KEP program organized and supported regional workshops, bringing together municipal officials responsible for environmental matters. These workshops not only provided a platform for knowledge exchange but also fostered improved communication and cooperation between central and local authorities in the realm of environmental law implementation.
Another vital aspect of the program's contribution was the assessment and restructuring of the existing framework within MESPI. This encompassed proposing changes, particularly with regard to the roles and competencies of various inspectorates, thus enhancing the efficiency of the institution. The KEP program has played an essential role in strengthening the institutional capacities of MESP and municipalities for the effective implementation of environmental legislation and regulations. Through various initiatives, assessments, and collaborative efforts, significant progress has been achieved in promoting environmental sustainability and ensuring compliance with international standards. This report showcases the commitment and dedication of all stakeholders involved in this important endeavor.
Component 6. Groundwater research in the Drini river basin
The primary focus of this component was in conducting comprehensive geophysical research and studies within the Drini i Bardhë river basin.
The KEP program initiated the process of opening 25 monitoring wells, conducting pumping tests, and systematically analyzing the results within the Drini i Bardhë river basin. The 25 wells were successfully completed and handed over to the Institute of Hydrogeological and Meteorological Institute of Kosovo for continuous monitoring and analysis.
The diligent execution of geophysical research and the subsequent establishment of monitoring wells represent significant strides in our quest to comprehensively understand the Drini i Bardhë river basin. These findings will undoubtedly play a vital role in the sustainable management and conservation of this vital natural resource.
Component 7. River Basin Management Plan for the Drini River Basin
The River Basin Management Plan (RBMP) for the Drini i Bardhë river basin, holds immense significance for Kosovo. It signifies a commitment to EU Directives implementation, support for the negotiation process, and fostering cooperation with neighboring countries on transboundary water management. This plan serves a multi-faceted role: it acts as a repository for assessed data, encompassing environmental objectives for surface and groundwater, water quality, quantity, and the impacts of human activities on water bodies, facilitates the coordination of various programs of measures and related initiatives within the river basin district.
The RBMP serves as the primary mechanism for reporting progress to the European Commission, in accordance with the Water Framework Directive, Article 15.
As the RBMP is a strategic document developed at the district level, the RBMA forms the basis for coordinating activities spanning analysis, planning, stakeholder engagement, and implementation across various geographic scales.
Component 8. Support for the Inter-ministerial Water Council (IMWC) through short-term mandates
This component provided support for the Inter-ministerial Council for Water, apart from the components of the Ministry. Jointly with IMWC the KEP updated the water strategy (approved version) and the Albanian-English-Albanian dictionary for water terminology supporting the water regulator. The KEP also conducted the report on drinking water.
Gender component
A crucial component of the Kosovo Environmental Program (KEP), embarked on an internal institutional gender analysis, titled "Creating Equal Opportunities." This landmark analysis, published in 2018, not only provided valuable insights but also yielded actionable recommendations to bolster gender equality within the Ministry.
The overarching objective of this gender analysis initiative was to delve deeply into the existing landscape of gender equality within the Ministry. This endeavor aimed to uncover potential gender disparities and elucidate their root causes. To accomplish this, we employed a comprehensive mixed-methods approach, synthesizing both quantitative and qualitative research methods for data collection and analysis. In the latter half of 2018, the Ministry took a significant step by establishing the Gender Group, comprising dedicated individuals from various departments. This strategic move aimed to enhance the integration of gender equality concerns at both organizational and operational levels.
In general, the achieved results in the Kosovo Environmental Program (KEP) show significant progress in various areas, including capacity building, biodiversity conservation, gender impact assessment, and transboundary cooperation.
Sustained political commitment and engagement with stakeholders will be vital to ensure the successful and sustainable improvement of Kosovo's environmental conditions and resilience to environmental and climate change issues.
